newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cricketer-politician hails Bhutto ouster.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cricketer-politician hails Bhutto ouster.

text.p: Imran Khan, Pakistan's cricketer-turned-politician, welcomed President Farooq Leghari's sacking of Benazir Bhutto as prime minister on Tuesday.

But Khan, one of the most popular politicians in the country, said his party would only fight parliamentary elections planned for February 3 if electoral reforms were implemented and a national census carried out.
"I feel that the decision to dismiss the government by the president was absolutely correct because the government had failed completely," Imran told Reuters Television in Lahore.
He was speaking after Leghari dissolved the National Assembly (lower house), removed Bhutto's government and named Meraj Khalid, 80, as caretaker prime minister.

"Politically, morally, in every way, the government had become ineffective," Imran said. "All the systems have broken down and above all corruption had reached a level where it was impossible for this government to function any more."
Imran, who founded his own Tehreek-e-Insaaf (Justice Movement) earlier this year, said his party had contributed to Bhutto's downfall by focusing attention on corruption.
He said those who had dipped their fingers into the national till should be brought to justice before the poll date announced by Leghari in his proclamation dismissing the government.
"Before the election there has to be accountability of those people who have robbed this country," he said.

The former Pakistan cricket captain, who married Anglo-French heiress Jemima Goldsmith last year, said the election commission had to be independent, a national census should be conducted and Pakistanis overseas allowed to vote.
"So if there are electoral reforms and if there is a census, I would be happy to fight an election tomorrow," he said.
Imran hailed Khalid's appointment as prime minister at the head of a three-month interim government as the "right choice".
"I feel he is one of the few politicians who is untainted and above who has done something for the country," he said.
Khalid is a former parliament speaker and longtime member of Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party who dissociated himself from active politics in 1993, the year Bhutto took office for the second time.
